searchText: I wonder if you switch 5% vals from one client to the other if you'll see a slashing, that could be a nice test of the slashing protection compatibilities they've been working on. Probably this can only be tried on LH<->Teku currently, but perhaps prysm soon. I tried to be careful with delays, checking temporary inactivity of stopped validators, and spot checks of which chain was being followed. There is a good effort going on for a standard slashing protection format, so you can move validators with no worries. But not quite there yet when doing it for all 4 clients, and many many nodes restarting the eth2stats server. All infra is still online I've been validating all night now and voted head incorrectly only four times, in all those slots, the block was proposed by Nimbus, seems like a big coincidence. potuz - which version are you running? we released a hotfix for this issue yesterday and will be making a full release today <@!203220829473996800> Confirmed, these are my bad head votes on another prysm key 13944, 13856,13664(prysm),13341,13239,12978,12941,12903,12836,12792 all those attested slots are proposed by Nimbus except the one marked prysm the odds of this happening are about 2^{-24} There's something going on perhaps with the block propagation on Nimbus nodes perhaps? <@!449019668296892420> I am running prysm but I am keeping track on which attestations I vote for the wrong head and they are all blocks that Nimbus proposed, this is very very unlikely and I think it is something to look into thanks! we'll track those down and see what the servers were up to at the time: https://github.com/status-im/nimbus-eth2/issues/2049 - we are planning an upgrade to some of the nodes that are running a validator count stress test Checking the third key and it looks exactly the same, all failed head votes are on Nimbus proposed blocks Restarting eth2stats server again. I believe it's leaking dead connections, need to review that code some time. we're restarting the nimbus fleet to give it a little performance boost regarding your issue <@!755590043632140352> , it does look like some of the blocks above were sent out a bit later than usual due to a cache miss - the better nodes will certainly help, but it looks like we can preseed the cache in this particular case Ah great, I'm glad that I wasn't just making noise as usual 😛 There's may be some kind of memory leak in the eth2stats server. Or it's getting too popular; collecting metrics and serving it of a over hundred nodes. Will try and get it back online soon. Eth2stats was under-resourced. Fixed that, updated DNS, and restarting its services. Should be back up soon, sorry for the inconvenience It's back up. As you might have to restart your eth2stats client, if it didn't pick up the change automatically
